title: A hex dump
description:
Show the bytes of any object, like a debugger's memory window.

```
00000000  48 65 6c 6c 6f 2c 20 58  65 6e 6f 6e 21 00 00 00  |Hello, Xenon!...|
00000010  2a 00 00 00                                       |*...|
```
hints: `std::printf("%02x ", bytes[i])` prints one byte as two hex digits. For the character column, a byte from 32 to 126 is printable and anything else shows as `.` (`std::isprint` from `<cctype>` makes the same test) (lesson 2.05).
Pad the last row with spaces so the character column lines up.
requirements: `void hexDump(const void* data, std::size_t size)` reads through `const unsigned char*`.
16 bytes per row: the offset, the bytes in hex with a gap after 8, then printable characters (others as `.`).
Dump a struct and an `int` and point out the little-endian order.
stretch: Highlight padding bytes in a struct by filling it with `0xAA` before setting the members.
